items_full.label: C275 · United Kingdom · 1992 · 5 pence · GBP

payload.story: A British five pence dated 1992, struck in cupronickel for everyday circulation. The obverse shows Raphael Maklouf's crowned portrait of Elizabeth II with the date in the legend. The reverse carries the crowned thistle design marked FIVE PENCE. The Royal Mint at Llantrisant struck about 453 million five pence coins in 1992.

record.mint: Royal Mint, Llantrisant (no mint mark on circulation)
record.metal: CuNi 75/25 · 3.25 g · 18 mm · milled
record.design: obverse Raphael Maklouf Elizabeth II · reverse crowned thistle · FIVE PENCE (Ironside)

payload.story: A 1977 Jamaican 10 cents bearing the national coat of arms: a crocodile crest above a shield flanked by two supporters, with the motto Out of Many, One People on the scroll below. A butterfly among flowers fills the other side. It was everyday small change in Jamaica in the late 1970s.

payload.story: A 1983 French 20 centimes, the golden everyday coin of pre-euro France. Marianne in her Phrygian cap of liberty is on the other side; the big 20 on this side sits inside a wreath of laurel and wheat.

items_full.label: C340 · Japan · 2015 · 100 yen · JPY

payload.story: A Japanese 100 yen coin dated Heisei 27 (2015). One side is filled with cherry blossoms, the sakura, Japan's beloved unofficial national flower; the other carries a big, plain 100. This design has served on the 100 yen since 1967, across three emperors.

items_full.label: C341 · German Democratic Republic · 1968 · 10 Pfennig · DDM

payload.story: An East German 10 pfennig from 1968, feather-light aluminium. One side carries the state emblem, a hammer and compass inside a wreath of wheat, ringed by the words Deutsche Demokratische Republik; the other has a big 10 over an oak leaf. Coins like this were the small change of the DDR until the state itself vanished in 1990.

record.mint: Berlin mint (A above the oak leaf on the value side)

items_full.label: C342 · South Korea · 2001 · 10 won · KRW

payload.story: A South Korean 10 won from 2001, struck in brass. The Dabotap pagoda of Bulguksa temple stands on one side, a stone pagoda from the 700s and one of Korea's national treasures, with the value in Hangul beside it. The other side carries a big 10, the year, and the Bank of Korea's name. This brass design ran from 1983 to 2006, when a smaller, cheaper copper-colored version took its place; the collection already holds that successor.

record.mint: Korea Minting and Security Printing Corporation, Daejeon (no mint mark)
